subject: maths
source: NCERT Ganita Prakash | Grade 6, Chapter 3 + BHPS midterm model paper (2026-27)

topics.name: Number line, digits and digit sums

questions.q: In the ‘taller neighbours’ game, a child says ‘2’ when…
questions.a: both children next to them are taller
questions.e: Each child says how many of their neighbours are taller.

questions.q: Can a child standing at the end of the line say ‘2’?
questions.a: No, they have only one neighbour
w: Only if they are the shortest
questions.e: An end child has just one neighbour, so the most they can say is 1.

questions.q: A cell is a ‘supercell’ if…
questions.a: its number is greater than all its neighbouring cells
w: its number is the largest in the table
it is in the middle of the row
questions.e: Compare with the cells immediately left, right (and top/bottom in a grid). (Model paper Q27a.)

questions.q: Will the cell with the largest number in a table always be a supercell?
questions.a: Yes, it is bigger than all its neighbours
w: Only if it is at the end
questions.e: The largest number beats every other number, including its neighbours.

questions.q: Can the cell with the smallest number be a supercell (in a table with more than one cell)?
questions.a: No, its neighbours are all bigger
w: Only if it is at the end
questions.e: The smallest number is smaller than its neighbours.

questions.q: How many 2-digit numbers are there?
What is the smallest number whose digit sum is 14?
questions.e: Use as few digits as possible and put the smaller digit first: 5 + 9 = 14 → 59.

questions.q: What is the largest 5-digit number whose digit sum is 14?
questions.e: Put the biggest digits first: 9 + 5 = 14, then zeros → 95000.

questions.q: Among the numbers 1–100, how many times does the digit 7 occur?
questions.e: Units place: 7, 17, …, 97 (10 times). Tens place: 70–79 (10 times). Total 20.

questions.q: On a number line from 1000 to 10,000 marked every 1000, where does 2754 lie?
questions.a: Between 2000 and 3000, closer to 3000
questions.e: 2754 is 754 past 2000 and only 246 before 3000.

questions.q: A palindrome is a number that…
questions.a: reads the same from left to right and from right to left
w: has an even number of digits
questions.e: 66, 848, 575, 1111 are palindromes.

questions.q: What is the smallest 5-digit palindrome?
questions.e: It must start and end with 1 and be as small as possible: 10001. (Model paper Q29.)

questions.q: What is the sum of the smallest and largest 5-digit palindromes?
What is the difference between the largest and smallest 5-digit palindromes?
How many 3-digit palindromes can be made using only the digits 1, 2 and 3 (repetition allowed)?
questions.e: First digit = last digit (3 choices) and middle digit (3 choices): 3 × 3 = 9.

questions.q: Puzzle: I am a 5-digit odd palindrome. My tens digit is double my units digit, and my hundreds digit is double my tens digit. Who am I?
questions.e: Units must be odd and small: units 1 → tens 2 → hundreds 4 → 12421.

questions.q: The time is 10:01. After how many minutes will a 12-hour clock next show a palindromic time?
questions.a: 70 minutes
questions.e: The next palindromic time is 11:11, which is 1 hour 10 minutes later.

questions.q: Start with 39, reverse and add until you get a palindrome: 39 + 93 = 132; 132 + 231 = ?
questions.e: 132 + 231 = 363, which is a palindrome.

questions.q: Which date is written as a palindrome (dd/mm/yyyy)?
questions.e: 11022011 reads the same both ways.

questions.q: The Kaprekar constant is…
questions.e: Repeating the routine on 4-digit numbers always reaches 6174.

questions.q: D. R. Kaprekar was…
questions.a: a mathematics teacher from Devlali, Maharashtra
questions.e: He discovered the 6174 pattern in 1949.

questions.q: For 3524, the largest and smallest numbers from its digits are…
questions.e: Arrange digits in descending then ascending order. (Model paper Q37a.)

questions.q: How many rounds does 3524 take to reach 6174?
The Kaprekar routine does NOT work for which number?
questions.e: You need at least two different digits; 3333 − 3333 = 0.

questions.q: For 3-digit numbers, the Kaprekar routine reaches which number?
Class sections have 32, 29 and 35 children. About how many children are in the class?
questions.a: About 100
questions.e: 32 + 29 + 35 = 96 ≈ 100. Round to easy numbers for estimates.

questions.q: ‘A 5-digit number + a 5-digit number gives a 5-digit number.’ This is…
questions.a: only sometimes true

questions.q: ‘A 4-digit number + a 2-digit number gives a 6-digit number.’ This is…
questions.a: never true
questions.e: The biggest possible sum is 9999 + 99 = 10,098, only 5 digits.

questions.q: ‘A 5-digit number − a 2-digit number gives a 3-digit number.’ This is…
questions.a: never true
w: true if the number is even
questions.e: The smallest result is 10,000 − 99 = 9901, a 4-digit number.
Group equal numbers and multiply.

questions.q: Collatz rule: if the number is even, ___; if it is odd, ___.
questions.a: halve it; multiply by 3 and add 1
questions.e: Repeat the rule until you reach 1. (Model paper Q35.)

questions.q: Collatz sequence starting with 21: 21, 64, 32, 16, … What comes after 16?
questions.e: 16 is even, so 16 ÷ 2 = 8. The sequence ends 8, 4, 2, 1. (Model paper Q35.)

questions.q: The Collatz conjecture says that…
questions.a: every starting number eventually reaches 1 – but nobody has proved it yet
w: it is proved for all numbers
questions.e: It is one of the most famous unsolved problems in mathematics (Lothar Collatz, 1937).

questions.q: Why does the Collatz conjecture hold for every power of 2 (2, 4, 8, 16, …)?
questions.a: Halving a power of 2 again and again always reaches 1
questions.e: 64 → 32 → 16 → 8 → 4 → 2 → 1: only halving is needed.

questions.q: In the game ‘21’ (say 1, 2 or 3 more each turn; first to reach 21 wins), which numbers should the winner say?
questions.e: Stay 4 apart: whatever the other player adds (1–3), you add the rest to make 4.

questions.q: A row of numbers reads 4, 9, 2, 7, 5, 8. How many supercells (bigger than all their neighbours) are there?
What is the greatest number of supercells possible in a row of {n} cells?
questions.e: Supercells cannot be neighbours, so every other cell: cells 1, 3, 5, … → {ans}.

questions.q: Can the smallest number in a row (of different numbers) be a supercell?
questions.a: No – it cannot be bigger than its neighbours
w: Only if it is at an end
Only in a row of 3 cells
questions.e: A supercell must be greater than every neighbour; the smallest number is less than all of them.

questions.q: What is the largest 4-digit number whose digits add up to 14?
questions.e: Put the biggest digits first: 9 + 5 + 0 + 0 = 14.

questions.q: What is the smallest 3-digit number whose digit sum is 20?
questions.e: Make the last digits as large as possible: 2 + 9 + 9 = 20.

questions.q: How many times is the digit 7 written when you write all the numbers from 1 to {N}?
questions.e: Every 100 numbers use 7 twenty times (10 in the ones place, 10 in the tens place): {ans}.

questions.q: How many 3-digit palindromes are there?
questions.e: First digit 1–9 (9 ways), middle digit 0–9 (10 ways): 9 × 10 = 90.

questions.q: Reverse-and-add: start with {n}. Add it to its reverse. What do you get after one step?
questions.e: {n} + its reverse = {ans}. Keep going until you reach a palindrome!

questions.q: On a 24-hour digital clock (hh:mm), which is the last palindromic time of the day?
questions.e: 23:32 reads the same backwards (2332).

questions.q: Which 4-digit numbers do NOT reach 6174 in Kaprekar’s process?
questions.a: Those with all four digits the same, like 3333
questions.e: 3333 − 3333 = 0, so the process stops at 0. Every other 4-digit number reaches 6174.

questions.q: At most how many steps does any 4-digit number (not all digits the same) take to reach 6174?
questions.e: Kaprekar found no number needs more than 7 steps.

questions.q: If you do Kaprekar’s process with 3-digit numbers, where do you end up?
Use 25 × 4 = 100 to work out 25 × {b} quickly.
Find the sum 1 + 2 + 3 + … + {n} quickly.
questions.e: Pair the ends: {n} × ({n} + 1) ÷ 2 = {ans}.

questions.q: Which is the best estimate of 4,987 × 21?
Collatz: start at {n}. If even, halve it; if odd, multiply by 3 and add 1. How many steps to reach 1?
questions.e: Write out every step and count them: {ans} steps.

questions.q: Which starting number reaches 1 in the fewest Collatz steps: 16, 15, 7 or 9?
questions.e: 16 → 8 → 4 → 2 → 1: just 4 steps (it is a power of 2).

questions.q: Has the Collatz conjecture been proved?
questions.a: No – it has been checked for huge numbers but never proved
questions.e: It remains one of the famous unsolved problems in mathematics.
